partner_context.their_ambition: Västtrafik is the public-transport authority for Västra Götaland, and it runs the ferries to Gothenburg's southern archipelago — the year-round public boats out of Saltholmen to Styrsö, Donsö and Vrångö. Västtrafik has a firm fossil-free target and has already trialled an electric hydrofoil in the archipelago. Its ambition on the water is fast, fossil-free island connectivity for the car-free islands its residents depend on.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the foiling-electric fleet for a network Västtrafik already runs and has already trialled on foils. The Saltholmen archipelago runs and the inter-island links — flown clear of the water: faster, near-silent, low-wake and zero-emission, on the same Västtrafik ticket, from the piers that already exist — an obvious next step from the electric-hydrofoil route trial the authority has already backed.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Gothenburg, Sweden · Västtrafik (Västra Götaland public transport)
hero.title: Navier × Gothenburg Ferries — the southern archipelago, on foils
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling layer on Västtrafik's southern-archipelago ferries — Saltholmen to Styrsö, Vrångö and beyond: faster, quieter and all-electric for the car-free islands Västtrafik already serves — and has already trialled on foils.
hero.what_we_do_together: Västtrafik brings the archipelago ferry network, the piers and the public-transport mandate — and a proven appetite for foiling; Navier brings the production foiling-electric fleet, captain training and the certification path. Together we run the same archipelago — faster and zero-emission — turning the authority's hydrofoil route trial into scheduled service.

why_now: Västtrafik has a fossil-free target and has already trialled an electric hydrofoil on an archipelago route, inside a country with a legislated net-zero-by-2045 goal. The intent is proven and the piers are in place; a production foiling-electric fleet is how the archipelago runs become fast and fossil-free at scale, with low wake through the car-free islands and their sensitive waters.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the Västtrafik network at Saltholmen, the tram-served gateway to the southern archipelago. A resident steps off tram 11 and straight onto a foil to Styrsö, Vrångö or Donsö — faster and fossil-free — while the conventional archipelago ferries keep the heaviest freight-and-vehicle runs underneath.

differentiation.why_navier: The platform is purpose-built for this network: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (vital on shared and protected waters), near-silent, zero-emission, and viable year-round. It delivers the authority's published decarbonisation commitment on the links where speed and wake have kept older vessels in service.

proof_points.claim: Västtrafik has already trialled a foiling ferry.
proof_points.evidence: Västtrafik backed an electric-hydrofoil route trial in the Gothenburg archipelago — a direct precedent for foiling public service.

proof_points.claim: The archipelago ferries are public transport.
proof_points.evidence: The Saltholmen southern-archipelago ferries (lines 281/282) run year-round on the Västtrafik public-transport ticket.
Sweden's climate framework legislates net-zero by 2045, with regional transport authorities driving fossil-free public transport.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: Can it run through a west-coast winter?
objections.response: The southern-archipelago ferries run year-round today; foiling-electric routing is planned around ice and weather, and the platform's efficiency suits the shoulder season especially well.

objections.concern: Does it disturb the car-free islands?
objections.response: The opposite — low wake and near-silent running reduce disturbance to the archipelago's sensitive waters and its car-free island communities.

objections.concern: Does this replace the ferries residents rely on?
objections.response: No — it's a faster, cleaner layer on the same Västtrafik ticket; conventional ferries keep the heaviest freight-and-vehicle runs.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path.
the_ask.partner_brings: The ferry route map, the piers/stops, the single-ticket integration, and the published decarbonisation mandate.
the_ask.next_step: Identify the first Västtrafik archipelago link — most likely Saltholmen–Styrsö — for a foiling-electric public pilot, building on the authority's own hydrofoil route trial.

close.body: Västtrafik has already put a foiling ferry on an archipelago route to see what's possible. Navier is how it becomes scheduled service — a fast, near-silent, fossil-free connection to Styrsö, Vrångö and the southern islands, on the same public ticket, and gentle on the archipelago's waters.
